title: Moses — The Red Sea
source: Exodus 14; visual adaptation of the biblical account
visualContinuity: Cinematic live-action biblical epic on an undeveloped Red Sea coast. Ancient Egyptian chariots and Hebrew refugees in plain earth-toned linen garments. Moses is an elderly Hebrew man with a long gray beard, deep maroon-red woven Levite robe with broad black stripes and narrow cream-white accent stripes and wooden staff. Natural human movement, realistic water and wind. Keep the crossing floor dry. No modern buildings, vehicles, clothing or electric lights. No dialogue or written text. Night progresses to dawn and morning. Drowning and aftermath are non-graphic. Do not depict Pharaoh himself drowning.

shots.prompt: Wide tracking shot along refugee families crowded on a sandy shoreline at night, hemmed in by dark turbulent sea. Adults carry bundles and guide children. Wind whips loose robes. The surf pounds loudly. Moonlit water fills the distance; fear and urgent movement.

Low moving camera beside Egyptian horse-drawn war chariots approaching the distant refugee camp at night. Wooden wheels turn rapidly, horses gallop and torch flames stream in the wind. Soldiers wear ancient bronze armor. Hooves and wheels thunder over dry ground.

Moses, an elderly gray-bearded man in a deep maroon-red Levite robe with broad black woven stripes and narrow cream-white accent stripes, stands with his wooden staff at the dark shoreline. Refugees move anxiously behind him. He turns toward the water, robe blowing in the strong wind. Slow lateral camera movement. Surf and wind, no speech.

A towering cloud moves from ahead of the Hebrew camp to behind it, separating the refugees from the pursuing Egyptians. The cloud casts deep darkness toward the chariots while warm firelight illuminates the refugees. Wide camera rises slowly as the cloud crosses between the two camps. Roaring wind.

Side silhouette of Moses at the waterline. He lifts his wooden rod and stretches his free hand over the sea. His maroon-and-black striped robe billows as the east wind strengthens. The water begins streaming away from the shore. Slow push toward his outstretched hand; wind and surf intensify.

Time-compressed wide view across the sea during the long night. Stars wheel overhead while a sustained powerful east wind drives the water back. The exposed ground broadens gradually between withdrawing masses of water. The shot visibly conveys hours passing through the night, with continuous rushing wind.

A vast corridor of dry seabed opens between towering walls of water on the right and left. Water surges within the walls while the passage stays dry. Camera advances slowly into the immense corridor from the near shore. Moonlight refracts through blue water; the wind roars.

The first Hebrew refugee families step from shore onto dry exposed seabed. A parent leads a child by the hand; others carry bundles. Tall water walls stand on both sides. Low camera tracks alongside their sandal-clad feet crossing firm dry ground. Footsteps and wind.

Moses is seen from behind walking with refugees through the dry passage, staff in hand, maroon-and-black striped Levite robe moving in the wind. Families and elders walk steadily around him. The camera follows at shoulder height between towering water walls. Human footsteps mingle with rushing water.

Very wide elevated view of a long column of Hebrew refugees crossing the sea on dry ground between two immense walls of water. The column moves toward the far shore as the first hint of dawn appears. Camera glides along the passage, emphasizing real walking motion and the scale of the crossing.

Egyptian chariots enter the dry sea passage in pursuit after the refugees. Horses pull the wooden vehicles between towering water walls. Soldiers look ahead toward the retreating column. Camera tracks beside a turning chariot wheel; fast hooves and rattling harnesses in the dim morning watch.

In the sea passage during the morning watch, a chariot wheel comes off its axle and rolls away. The vehicle lurches and slows; nearby Egyptian charioteers struggle in confusion and try to turn back. Ground remains dry. Close moving camera follows the loose wheel, then reveals halted chariots. Cracking wood and frightened horses.

The last Hebrew families hurry out of the dry passage onto the far shore as dawn brightens. People help an elder climb the sandy bank, then move clear of the waterline. Moses watches from the safe shore, staff at his side. Camera tracks backward with the refugees; hurried footsteps and heavy breathing.

From the far shore in morning light, Moses stretches his hand back over the sea. Show him in profile and then the vast passage beyond his outstretched arm. Refugees stand safely behind him. The water walls begin to shudder. A slow camera push accompanies the deepening rumble.

Inside the sea passage, Egyptian soldiers and charioteers see the towering water walls folding inward. They turn and struggle to flee among damaged chariots. Camera retreats ahead of them as sheets of water begin falling from both sides. Rising roar, splashing horses, urgent human movement, no gore.

Wide cinematic view as the returning sea crashes over the pursuing Egyptian army and its chariots. Soldiers and horses are engulfed beneath the immense collapsing water. Show the overwhelming force and drowning without close-up injuries or gore. The dry corridor disappears completely beneath surging waves. Thunderous water.

Morning aftermath on the shoreline. Waves wash broken chariot wood and abandoned shields onto wet sand beside motionless Egyptian soldiers, seen at a respectful distance without wounds or gore. The sea has returned to its normal course. Slow lateral camera and subdued surf make the army's death clear.

Wide closing shot of the surviving Hebrew refugees safely gathered above the far shore in morning sunlight. Moses stands among them with his wooden staff, seen from behind. They look across the restored sea. Robes move gently in the easing wind as the camera slowly pulls back. Calm surf, quiet breathing, solemn relief.
